Provenance.drafts: Seed 714010, batch of 4 at 896x1152. #1 read as a squat cottage with no smithy identity below the arch; #2 put the forge mouth behind a porch that would hide it at draw size; #3 shipped a lit backdrop panel baked into the frame. #4 - the tallest silhouette, ember arch reading clearly at the ground floor, chimney and roof separating cleanly from the backdrop - was the winner and needed no inpaint.
Provenance.aiDisclosure: AI-generated (SDXL base 1.0 + pixel-art-xl LoRA at 0.9/0.9) diffuse, one ComfyUI KSampler pass at 896x1152, seed 714010, dpmpp_2m/karras, 30 steps, cfg 7.0, batch of 4. IPAdapter (vit-h, style transfer, weight 0.9) referenced market.png so palette and lighting lock to the Shop the owner named as art he likes -- the same chain this file recorded for the previous render, re-run rather than reinvented. Cropped to the alpha box, BOX-downsampled straight to the target height, and padded 1px of transparency on every side (VenueArtContractTests assertion 1). Sized to 170px = 5.00x the tallest resolved character body, ranked by role inside R14.8's 3.5-5.5x band rather than scaled uniformly: a uniform multiplier would have left the smaller buildings still undersized, which is the complaint (#142) still open. Replaces the render this file previously described, which measured 1.41-2.59x and is what made the heroes look too big for the town. DEVIATION from cutout.py: the alpha is cut by art/pipeline/gen-venues-r14.py's own deterministic border-seeded flood fill against the border-median reference colour, not the BiRefNet model cutout.py wraps -- these renders put the subject on a near-flat backdrop, where a segmentation pass buys nothing and a reproducible 40-line function buys a --cut flag that regenerates the committed pixels byte-for-byte. cutout.py/BiRefNet remains the tool of record for gradient or busy backgrounds.
